questions.q: What four things does a usable glossary definition state, per this lesson's four-part test?
options: What the term is, what it explicitly excludes, how it's measured, and who approved it
The term's length, color, and font
The server name, database name, and schema name
Only a one-word synonym for the term
questions.explain: The lesson defines the four-part test as stating what the term is, what it excludes, how it's measured, and who approved it.

questions.q: Why does LTV Global's 'Customer' definition explicitly exclude a Beacon lead with no completed order?
options: Because that kind of record is a Prospect, a distinct term, and conflating the two is exactly the ambiguity the four-part test exists to prevent
Because Beacon records are never real people
Because Prospects and Customers are identical in every way
Because the lesson has no rule about exclusions
questions.explain: The definition explicitly names 'Prospect' as the excluded neighbor term, keeping Customer scoped to people with a completed order.

questions.q: Why does the dictionary pull column facts from INFORMATION_SCHEMA rather than writing them from memory?
options: It returns the real, current structural facts — type, length, nullability — which is faster and more accurate than guessing
INFORMATION_SCHEMA is a marketing tool, not a metadata source
Memory-based documentation is always more accurate than querying the schema
INFORMATION_SCHEMA only works for the Products table
questions.explain: The lesson shows a real INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS query specifically because it returns accurate, current structural facts about the real tables.

questions.q: What does 'Order Total' explicitly exclude, per the glossary entry in this lesson?
options: Comet's Cart Value, the pre-checkout subtotal before tax and shipping
Any order placed outside the United States
Orders placed by returning customers
Orders that include more than one product
questions.explain: The Order Total definition names Cart Value as the excluded neighbor term — Comet's pre-tax, pre-shipping subtotal, calculated before checkout.

questions.q: What does each data dictionary row ultimately pair together, per this lesson?
options: The real column's structural facts (type, nullability) with the glossary term that gives it business meaning
Two completely unrelated tables
A column's name with a random number
The system's uptime with its hosting cost
questions.explain: The lesson's dictionary table pairs each real column (e.g. dbo.Orders.OrderTotal) with the glossary term that defines what it means in business terms.
